newsitem.title: USA: Dow cleared in Mich. breast implant claims.
newsitem.headline: Dow cleared in Mich. breast implant claims.

text.p: A Wayne County Circuit judge ruled Thursday that Dow Chemical Co should not be held liable for the medical problems alleged by hundreds of Michigan women who have silicone gel breast implants.

The ruling by Circuit Court Judge Robert Colombo marks the third time a state court judge has ruled against plaintiffs suing the Midland, Mich., based chemical company, said David Black, one of the lead plaintiff attorneys in the Michigan case.
Black said the Michigan plaintiffs may appeal the ruling.

Dow Corning is jointly owned Dow Chemical and Corning Inc. Once the world's largest maker of breast implants filled with silicone gel, Dow Corning filed for U.S. Bankruptcy Court protection two years ago because of the potential legal claims it was facing.
Thousands of women with the implants allege they suffer from connective tissue and immune system problems.

Appellate courts in New York and California have upheld lower court rulings that dismiss Dow Chemical from liability. The company said the Michigan decision affects about 800 cases filed against it in the state. The company said it has been dismissed from more than 3,000 silicone implant cases.

Colombo's action was the second time he dismissed Michigan claims against Dow Chemical. After Colombo's first decision in April 1994, U.S. District Court Judge Sam Pointer, who is overseeing all federal breast implant cases, amended an earlier ruling that opened the door for plaintiffs to refile their state claims.

Plaintiff attorney Black said plaintiffs did just that by amending the original master complaint. Unless Colombo's ruling is reversed, Black said it likely Michigan women will only have the bankruptcy case to seek legal remedies.
"Naturally, the plaintiffs are disappointed," said Black. "I'm sure we're going to seriously look at filing an appeal to the Michigan Court of Appeals."
According to Dow Chemical, the judge rejected plaintiff claims that implant maker Dow Corning Corp relied on Dow Chemical to establish the safety of silicone-filled implants for medical use.
Dow Chemical did not manufacture silicone for the implants, although it says it did conduct silicone tests for Dow Corning that were unrelated to breast implants.
